items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: And myself and Joe Thomas on trumpet, and it was a good date.

ctx.x: We were talking on the last reel the record date in which Cozy was the leader. about (inaudible).

That's right. This was a date Harry put together in New York, and Cozy was leader on it, and, as I mentioned, four of the guy -- guys in the group was Coleman Hawkins, Earl Hines, Billy Taylor on bass -- he's a bass player. I think he retired. He played with Duke once. And myself and Joe Thomas on trumpet, and it was a good date. We did one song I wrote, was "Through for the Night." And then we did Blue Moon, and then we featured Earl and Coleman Hawkins on "Just One More Chance." And I don't remember what -- I…

items.title: 73243_Joe Thomas oral history interview
items.q: session you did with Hawk, Trummy and Earl

ctx.x: It's ridiculous. It's ridiculous because in the first place if you do those kind of things, as we did, you don't have full expression yourself. If music is anything, it's expression.
Well, now we never mentioned some of the great records of all time I think was that session you did with Hawk, Trummy and Earl. That's a beautiful record.
That was Twelve o'clock at night.
